title: BP to cut stakes in flagship U.K. carbon capture projects
content:
[BP Filling Station Signage]
Oli Scarff/Getty Images News

BP (BP [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BP]) said Thursday it plans to sell down its stakes [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/climate-energy/bp-sell-stakes-flagship-uk-carbon-capture-projects-northern-england-2026-05-07/] in two flagship U.K. carbon capture and storage projects, the Northern Endurance Partnership project and the Net Zero Teesside Power project in northern ​England, without disclosing the size of the stakes on ⁠offer or potential buyers.

"As the NZT ​Power and NEP projects have reached major milestones, including financial ​close and the start of construction, BP considers this the right time to sell a portion of its equity in both projects," the company said in a statement to Reuters.

BP (BP [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BP]) partners with Equinor (EQNR [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/EQNR]) and TotalEnergies (TTE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TTE]) in the NEP project, which is expected to permanently store ​up to ​an initial 4M metric tons/year of carbon dioxide, and with Equinor in the NZT power project, which is poised to be the ​world's ⁠first gas power plant with carbon capture and deliver power to ~1M U.K. homes from ⁠2028.

Separately, the U.S. has extended [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/us-extends-bp-license-azeri-gas-field-bp-says-2026-05-07/] ​a license allowing ‌BP (BP [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/BP]) to continue to operate its ​Shah Deniz ​natural gas field in ⁠Azerbaijan with Iranian ​and Russian partners, ​the company said Thursday.

title: Equinor (OB:EQNR) Is Up 6.0% After Record Output And Higher EPS Lift Q1 2026 Results
content:
Equinor reported first‑quarter 2026 results with revenue of US$27,843 million versus US$29,920 million a year earlier, while net income rose to US$3,106 million and basic earnings per share from continuing operations increased to US$1.24 from US$0.97. Alongside record production, Equinor extended about US$1.80 billion of drilling and well services contracts and confirmed further dividends and share buybacks, underlining its focus on sustaining output and capital returns while filing a new universal shelf to keep funding options open. Now we’ll examine how this combination of record output, stronger earnings, and extended drilling contracts affects Equinor’s earlier investment narrative.

Equinor Investment Narrative Recap

To own Equinor, you essentially have to believe in its ability to convert a large, mostly gas‑weighted production base into resilient cash flows while managing energy transition and price volatility. The latest quarter delivered higher earnings and record output despite lower revenue, which supports the near term earnings story. The biggest near term catalyst remains operational delivery on growth projects, while a key risk is that weaker commodity prices or higher costs could quickly compress already modest profit margins.

The Q1 2026 earnings announcement is particularly relevant here, as it pairs record production of more than 2.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day with continued dividends and buybacks. That combination reinforces the existing catalyst of disciplined capital returns, but it also sharpens the risk that Equinor is leaning on shareholder distributions at a time when analysts already expect only low single digit annual earnings growth and slightly declining revenue.
